cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Monogamy – the practice or state of having a relationship with only one partner at a time.

p.em: Example: She wondered if her lifelong attachment to cultural habits was a form of social monogamy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Heritage – valued objects and qualities such as cultural traditions that have been passed down from previous generations.

p.em: Example: Our city has a rich architectural heritage that we must protect for our children.

cosy-blockquote.p: Devotion – love, loyalty, or enthusiasm for a person, activity, or cause.

p.em: Example: His absolute devotion to keeping the old winter festival alive was admirable.

cosy-blockquote.p: Heirloom – a valuable object that has belonged to a family for several generations.

p.em: Example: The silver teapot was an heirloom that carried decades of family memories.

cosy-blockquote.p: Preserve – to maintain something in its original or existing state.

p.em: Example: It is difficult to preserve physical books in humid weather without special equipment.

cosy-blockquote.p: Conformity – compliance with standards, rules, or laws.

p.em: Example: Young people often rebel against the strict conformity of traditional hometowns.

cosy-blockquote.p: Obligation – an act or course of action to which a person is morally or legally bound; a duty.

p.em: Example: Celebrating holidays together shouldn't feel like a heavy family obligation.

cosy-blockquote.p: Customary – according to the customs or usual practices associated with a particular society.

p.em: Example: It is customary to thank the host before leaving a traditional dinner party.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nostalgia – a sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past.

p.em: Example: Listening to old jazz songs always fills her with a sweet sense of nostalgia.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ritual – a series of actions performed according to a prescribed order.

p.em: Example: Making fresh coffee in the morning has become a comforting personal ritual.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do we feel a deep devotion to family traditions we didn't choose, even when they are believed to limit our freedom?
★ Have you ever felt pressured to participate in a holiday custom that felt completely arbitrary to you?

Is preserving a vintage family heirloom considered to be a way to find stability, or is it just living in the past?
★ What is the oldest physical heirloom in your family, and is it said to have a special story?

It is often said that society demands too much conformity through traditional wedding and career timelines.
★ Have you ever decided to skip a standard social milestone to do something different?

Can we protect our cultural heritage if we are expected to show blind devotion to outdated rules?
★ Is there a special family ritual from your childhood that you still practice today?

In what ways do family obligations turn simple customs into a 'social monogamy' where exploring alternative lifestyles is seen as a betrayal?
★ Have you ever felt like a rebel just for wanting to try a different way of celebrating a holiday?

When we blindly inherit our ancestors' belief systems, is it thought to be a sign of respect or just letting dead people rule our lives?
★ Do you still follow old family rules even when they make no sense today?

Why is it customary to feel guilty when we prioritize personal solitude over a traditional family gathering?
★ How do you deal with family members who insist that you attend every single holiday dinner?

If cultural habits are treated with the same commitment as marital monogamy, are other cultures' rituals believed to threaten our own identity?
★ Have you ever preferred another culture's holiday customs over those of your own family?

A strong sense of nostalgia is known to help people cope with the fast-paced, unpredictable nature of modern life.
★ What is one modern daily habit you would like to pass down to your children?

How do we separate a comforting ritual that brings people together from a social obligation that keeps us trapped?
★ In your opinion, is social conformity considered to be essential for a stable society?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Traditional societies are believed to have found deep meaning in collective rituals, while modern urbanites are said to suffer from fleeting, meaningless trends.
★ Do you prefer modern lifestyle flexibility, or do you sometimes wish for simpler, predefined social roles?

Passing down a physical family heirloom is thought to keep family history alive, whereas digital archives are believed to lack real soul.
★ Would you rather inherit an ancient piece of furniture or a journal written by your great-grandparents?

While older generations were expected to follow a strict customary timeline for marriage, modern life is said to offer an overwhelming number of choices.
★ Do you feel that having so many lifestyle options today makes it harder to find happiness?

Ancient communities are known to have had a monopoly on what they considered to be the truth, whereas modern multicultural cities force us to compromise.
★ Do you prefer a highly diverse neighborhood, or do you find a more traditional, uniform community easier to live in?

Traditional life is said to have relied on a lifelong commitment to the soil, while modern globalization is believed to turn us into geographic nomads.
★ If you have moved to different cities, did it make you feel more independent or more isolated?

In the past, showing reverence for heritage was considered to be the foundation of social order, but modern culture is said to celebrate the rebel.
★ Do you admire people who completely ignore traditions and build their own rules from scratch?

Traditional marriage was believed to be a pragmatic economic contract, while modern romance is thought to be an intense search for self-actualization.
★ Do you think modern relationships fail more often because we expect too much from our partners?

Outdated laws were once protected in the name of sacred tradition, whereas modern secular societies are considered to be more willing to discard outdated rules.
★ What outdated tradition are you happiest to see disappearing from the modern world?

While past generations fought desperately to preserve ancestral buildings, modern cities are believed to prioritize constant demolition.
★ How do you feel when vintage historic buildings in your town are demolished to build modern glass towers?

Traditional systems are said to have created a comforting but rigid social structure, while modern freedom is thought to leave many feeling utterly isolated.
★ Would you give up a little bit of your privacy if it meant being part of a super-supportive community?
